Why, that's the way To fool their preparation, and to conquer Their most absurd intents.
Re-enter CHARMIAN.
Now, Charmian! Show me, my women, like a queen: go fetch My best attires: I am again for Cydnus, To meet Mark Antony: sirrah Iras, go. Now, noble Charmian, we'll dispatch indeed; And, when thou hast done this chare, I'll give
thee leave To play till doomsday. Bring our crown and all. Wherefore's this noise ?
Exit Iras. A noise within.
Enter a Guardsman.

sp.speaker: Guard.
sp.p: Here is a rural fellow That will not be denied your highness' presence: He brings you figs.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p:
Let him come in. Exit Guardsman.
What poor an instrument May do a noble deed! he brings me liberty. My resolution's placed, and I have nothing Of woman in me: now from head to foot I am marble-constant; now the fleeting moon No planet is of mine.
Re-enter Guardsman, with Clown bringing in
a basket.

sp.speaker: Guard.
sp.p: This is the man.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p:
Avoid, and leave him.
Exit Guardsman. Hast thou the pretty worm of Nilus there, That kills and pains not ?

sp.speaker: Clown.
sp.p: Truly, I have him: but I would not be the party that should desire you to touch him, for his biting is immortal; those that do die of it do seldom or never recover.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p:
Rememberest thou any that have died
on't ?

sp.speaker: Clown.
sp.p: Very many, men and women too. I heard of one of them no longer than yesterday: a very honest woman, but something given to lie; as a woman should not do, but in the way of honesty: how she died of the biting of it, what pain she felt: truly, she makes a very good report o' the worm; but he that will believe all that they say, shall never be saved by half that they do: but this is most fallible, the worm's an odd worm.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p: Get thee hence; farewell.

sp.speaker: Clown.
sp.p:
I wish you all joy of the worm.
Setting down his basket.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p: Farewell.

sp.speaker: Clown.
sp.p: You must think this, look you, that the worm will do his kind.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p: Ay, ay; farewell.

sp.speaker: Clown.
Cleo.
sp.p: Take thou no care; it shall be heeded.

sp.speaker: Clown.
sp.p: Very good. Give it nothing, I pray you, for it is not worth the feeding.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p: Will it eat me ?

sp.speaker: Clown.
sp.p: You must not think I am so simple but I know the devil himself will not eat a woman: I know that a woman is a dish for the gods, if the devil dress her not. But, truly, these same whoreson devils do the gods great harm in their women; for in every ten that they make, the devils mar five.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p: Well, get thee gone; farewell.

sp.speaker: Clown.
sp.p:
Yes, forsooth: I wish you joy o' the worm. Exit.
Re-enter IRAS with a robe, crown, &c.

sp.speaker: Cleo.
Char.
sp.p:
Dissolve, thick cloud, and rain; that I
may say, The gods themselves do weep!

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p:
This proves me base: If she first meet the curled Antony, He'll make demand of her, and spend that kiss Which is my heaven to have. Come, thou
mortal wretch,
To an asp, which she applies to her breast. With thy sharp teeth this knot intrinsicate Of life at once untie: poor venomous fool, Be angry, and dispatch. O, couldst thou speak, That I might hear thee call great Cæsar ass Unpolicied!

sp.speaker: Char.
sp.p: O eastern star!

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p: Peace, peace! Dost thou not see my baby at my breast, That sucks the nurse asleep ?

sp.speaker: Char.
sp.p: O, break ! O, break !

sp.speaker: Cleo.
sp.p:
As sweet as balm, as soft as air, as
gentle,— O Antony !—Nay, I will take thee too.
Applying another asp to her arm. What should I stay— Dies.

sp.speaker: Char.
sp.p:
In this vile world? So, fare thee well. Now boast thee, death, in thy possession lies A lass unparalleled. Downy windows, close; And golden Phoebus never be beheld Of eyes again so royal! Your crown's awry; I'll mend it, and then play.
Enter the Guard, rushing in.

sp.speaker: First Guard.
sp.p: Where is the queen ?

sp.speaker: Char.
sp.p: Speak softly, wake her not.

sp.speaker: First Guard.
sp.p: Cæsar hath sent—

sp.speaker: Char.
sp.p:
Too slow a messenger.
Applies an asp. O, come apace, dispatch ! I partly feel thee.

sp.speaker: First Guard.
sp.p:
Approach, ho! All's not well:
Cæsar's beguiled.

sp.speaker: Sec. Guard.
sp.p:
There's Dolabella sent from
Cæsar; call him.

sp.speaker: First Guard.
sp.p:
What work is here! Charmian,
is this well done?

sp.speaker: Char.
sp.p:
It is well done, and fitting for a
princess Descended of so many royal kings. Ah, soldier ! Dies.
Re-enter DOLABELLA.

sp.speaker: Dol.
sp.p: How goes it here ?

sp.speaker: Sec. Guard.
sp.p: All dead.

sp.speaker: Dol.
sp.p:
Cæsar, thy thoughts Touch their effects in this: thyself art coming To see perform'd the dreaded act which thou So sought'st to hinder.
Within 'A way there, a way for Cæsar!'
Re-enter CÆSAR and all his train marching.

sp.speaker: Dol.
sp.p: O sir, you are too sure an augurer; That you did fear is done.

sp.speaker: Cæs.
sp.p: Bravest at the last, She levell'd at our purposes, and, being royal, Took her own way. The manner of their deaths ? I do not see them bleed.

sp.speaker: Dol.
sp.p: Who was last with them ?

sp.speaker: First Guard.
sp.p:
A simple countryman, that
brought her figs: This was his basket.

sp.speaker: Cæs.
sp.p: Poison'd, then.

sp.speaker: First Guard.
sp.p:
O Cæsar, This Charmian lived but now; she stood and
spake: I found her trimming up the diadem On her dead mistress; tremblingly she stood And on the sudden dropp'd.

sp.speaker: Cæs.
sp.p: O noble weakness ! If they had swallow'd poison, 'twould appear By external swelling: but she looks like sleep, As she would catch another Antony In her strong toil of grace.

sp.speaker: Dol.
sp.p: Here, on her breast, There is a vent of blood and something blown: The like is on her arm.

sp.speaker: First Guard.
sp.p:
This is an aspic's trail: and
these fig-leaves Have slime upon them, such as the aspic leaves Upon the caves of Nile.

sp.speaker: Cæs.
sp.p: Most probable That so she died; for her physician tells me She hath pursued conclusions infinite Of easy ways to die. Take up her bed; And bear her women from the monument: She shall be buried by her Antony: No grave upon the earth shall clip in it A pair so famous. High events as these Strike those that make them; and their story is No less in pity than his glory which Brought them to be lamented. Our army shall In solemn show attend this funeral; And then to Rome. Come, Dolabella, see High order in this great solemnity. Exeunt.
